headline: Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech flips Sept from 25bp cut to 60% odds of a hike
summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole debut argued 'underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved' and that 'broad financial conditions' cannot be described as restrictive, reaffirming 2% PCE as the firm target. By Monday morning fed funds futures priced a 60.4% probability of a 25bp HIKE at the Sept 16-17 FOMC, up from ~35% Friday morning; the 2-year note added ~8bps to 4.31%, the highest since late July. That is a full ~140bp swing in policy expectations from Friday's post-PCE pricing (which had a 25bp CUT at ~83%). High-beta AI/tech and rate-sensitive utilities are most exposed to the repricing.

headline: US strikes Iranian launchers near Strait of Hormuz Sunday; Iran hits US bases in Jordan and UAE
summary: US Central Command struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island preparing to seed mines in the Strait of Hormuz Sunday - the first US military action in the region in a month. Iran's Revolutionary Guards retaliated with missile strikes on US bases in Jordan and the UAE. Brent crude jumped ~2.5% to $90.27/bbl in Monday trading (session high $91.52, highest since Aug 25); WTI printed $85.77 (+2.84%). Roughly 6-8M bbl/day still flowing through Hormuz. The escalation adds a supply-shock overlay to Warsh's hawkish inflation signal - a hawkish Fed and rising oil is the worst combination for AI-infra multiples.

headline: Samsung locks 70% of HBM capacity to Microsoft, Nvidia, Google through 2031 at ~$300-400/module
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports Samsung has committed ~70% of its HBM production capacity through 2031 under long-term agreements with Microsoft, Nvidia and Google, pricing modules at $300-$400 vs $2,100 on the spot market - an ~80% discount for multi-year visibility. Complements SK Hynix's $38.3B HBM capex plan through 2031 and its Indiana packaging groundbreaking last week. Counterpoint's 2026 HBM4 share forecast: SK Hynix 54%, Samsung 28%, Micron 18%. Read-through: memory shortage extends well past 2030 per SK Hynix CEO, and the buyer LTAs de-risk supply for the hyperscaler capex cycle while pushing spot-market entrants toward Micron.

headline: Broadcom fiscal Q3 earnings Wednesday AMC - $16B AI-semi guide is the tape mover
summary: AVGO reports fiscal Q3 after the close Wed Sept 2. Consensus: $29.43B revenue (+84% YoY) and $2.55 GAAP EPS; guide is $29.4B rev and $16.0B AI semiconductors (+200%+ YoY). Setup is sensitive: after Q2 on June 3 the stock fell -12.6% in a single session despite a beat because management declined to raise the FY27 AI-semi target above the prior 'in excess of $100B'. Watch for any upward revision to the FY27 number and for commentary on the BofA-flagged $370B AI-financing debt path to 2029. Reports the same afternoon as HPE.

headline: Dell fiscal Q2 2027 earnings Tuesday AMC - Street eyes $45B revenue, $4.91 EPS on $43B AI backlog
summary: DELL reports fiscal Q2 2027 after the close Tue Sept 1. Consensus revenue $45.1B (~50% growth) and non-GAAP EPS $4.91, more than 2x YoY. Full-year FY27 outlook stands at $165-169B (+47% YoY) with AI-Optimized Server revenue guided to ~$60B (+144% YoY) and Q2 ISG segment guided +75%. Q1 FY27 booked $24.4B AI orders and recognized $16.1B AI-server revenue; the $43B AI backlog print and any guide raise are the tape movers. Stock is +272% YTD - the buy-the-rumor is fully in.

headline: HPE fiscal Q3 earnings Wednesday AMC - $12B revenue guide anchored on AI-infra networking mix
summary: HPE reports fiscal Q3 2026 after close Wed Sept 2. Company guide is $11.5-12.1B revenue with $0.88-0.93 non-GAAP EPS; Zacks consensus $12.1B/$0.94 (+32% rev, +114% EPS YoY). Growth is driven by the Juniper networking mix, AI-inferencing/agentic-AI compute demand, and data-intensive workloads. Reports concurrent with AVGO - back-to-back AI-hardware tape gates the sector into the Fri jobs print.

headline: KOSPI recovers +0.46% to 6,820 as Samsung and SK Hynix rebound intraday; foreigners sold >1T won
summary: Kospi opened weak on Warsh's Jackson Hole hawkish shift and the US-Iran Hormuz escalation, dropping to an intraday low of 6,617 (-2.53%) before recovering through the afternoon on chip-name buying to close at 6,820.02 (+0.46%). Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rebounded off session lows despite foreign investors offloading more than 1 trillion won on the main board. The Kospi setup remains constructive for HBM/AI beta but the flow signals net-de-risking into the Broadcom/Dell prints and the Sept 5 US NFP.

headline: Marvell sell-side hikes price targets across the board despite Friday's -8% AH selloff
summary: Following MRVL's beat-and-raise Q2 FY27 print, sell-side desks raised or reiterated bullish price targets: Craig-Hallum lifted PT to $300 from $217 (+38%) and kept Buy on the FY27 rev guide bump to ~$12B and FY28 to ~$18B, with data-center revenue set to grow >60% both years. TD Cowen raised PT to $245 from $225 (Hold). BofA reiterated Buy $365, UBS reiterated Buy $310, Barclays and Citi reiterated $275, Wells Fargo Overweight $310. Stock still traded down 10% intraday Friday on valuation as MRVL was +184% YTD into the print.

headline: Meta Hyperion (Louisiana) datacenter ramps to 3,700 workers en route to 5,000; Sept LPSC hearing on Babel-Webre 500kV line
summary: Construction of Meta's $10B Hyperion supercluster in Richland Parish LA is scaling toward 5,000 workers on site from 3,700 currently. The site's ultimate capacity targets 2GW and could expand to 5GW - equivalent to the power draw of 4M homes. Entergy has proposed three new gas plants ($3B) to serve the load; the enabling Babel-Webre 500kV transmission line has an LPSC hearing scheduled for Sept 2026 with a targeted Q4 2026 decision. Read-through: near-term catalyst for ETN (T&D switchgear), GEV/SIE (gas turbines - both back-ordered into 2031/2029), and gas midstream. Meta is one of the largest corporate nuclear buyers globally with 6.6GW of contracted capacity across VST/CEG/OKLO/TerraPower.

headline: Chicago manufacturing PMI misses at 47.1 vs 58 expected; consumer sentiment falls to 51.7
summary: August Chicago manufacturing PMI printed 47.1 vs consensus 58 - a major miss keeping the index in contraction. Consumer sentiment slid to 51.7 from July's 55.2. Combined with Warsh's hawkish rhetoric this is stagflationary at the margin - softening growth data alongside sticky inflation warnings, which is historically the toughest macro backdrop for high-multiple AI/AI-infra names. Focus now shifts to Friday's Sept 5 NFP as the last major macro gate before the Sept 16-17 FOMC.
